name: subscription.refresh
title: Fetch subscription feeds into Servers
summary: Fetch, guard, parse, move every credential into the keystore, then hand reference-shaped Servers back -- never delete-on-error. The fetch is Connector-side because only the Connector writes the keystore (no keystore.put in the allowlist), so a feed body of user UUIDs and tokens has no other route (docs/architecture/29 §2). Keeps the legacy sha256 compare and keep-last-good path (docs/audit/09).

sources.description: The SubscriptionSource documents exactly as the extension owns them, passed whole rather than by identifier: the Connector keeps no copy of user intent (ADR-0010, docs/architecture/34) and therefore cannot look a source up. It reads `url` or the address behind `urlRef`, `headersRef`, `format`, `limits` and the backoff in `status`; it writes none of them back -- the result is not a mutated source, with exactly one exception: `refreshed[].format` is the value an `auto` declaration resolved to, and the extension persists it into the source it owns (`docs/architecture/34-data-split.md` §6), so `auto` never survives into a stored source. No other source field is ever written back. Two entries with the same `id` in one call is a `BadRequest`: two fetches for one source would race its keystore entries and its hash.

force.description: Ignore the `status.nextAttemptAt` backoff carried by each source. Rate-limited per sender by the Connector so that a UI defect cannot hammer a feed (docs/architecture/31).

sha256.description: Hash of the raw body as received, before parsing. The extension stores it as `status.lastSha256`, which is what makes the next call's `unchanged` verdict reproducible without the Connector remembering anything.

format.description: The format the parser's detector resolved the body to -- the answer an `auto` declaration hid, and the one source field the result carries back: the extension writes it into the source it owns (`docs/architecture/34-data-split.md` §6), so `auto` never survives into a stored source (`docs/architecture/29-subscriptions-and-servers.md` §5). The enum is the source schema's minus `auto`: a resolved format is by definition not the declaration that deferred the choice. A body two detectors claim is not a value here but a failed entry: `SchemaMismatch` naming both.

duplicates.description: Entries that collapsed onto an identity this source already had. Counted, never silently merged (docs/architecture/29 §6).

lossyFields.description: Fields the input format could not carry (see the loss table in docs/architecture/29 §5). The UI must ask rather than guess, and MUST NOT invent a transport for a server whose transport the feed did not state.

servers.description: The parsed Servers, every credential already moved into the keystore and replaced by a `keystore://` reference. Validated against `server.schema.json` before this frame is emitted, which is the machine-checkable proof that extraction ran: a Server carrying a value fails the schema, so an un-extracted secret cannot be shipped to the extension at all. The extension persists these under `-nexora.server.<id>` and passes the ids to `config.apply`.

unchanged.description: Sources whose body hash equals the `status.lastSha256` supplied in the request. Not a failure, and not a refresh: the extension updates `status.lastAttemptAt` only, and the servers are NOT resent.

partialServers.description: Only with `QuotaExceeded` or a per-entry `SchemaMismatch`: the servers that DID parse, so the UI can show what was dropped instead of pretending nothing arrived. Empty for transport failures -- a source that never answered has nothing to report, and its last good set stays untouched.

skipped.description: Backoff not yet elapsed, or a refresh for this source already running. Distinct from `failed` so that a caller cannot read 'skipped' as success.

invariants: A failed refresh leaves the last good Server set byte-identical and still usable (LIVE-12).
An HTTP 404 never deletes a subscription; removal is an explicit user action.
Every credential from a feed body lands in the keystore and every Server in the result validates against server.schema.json unchanged.
No subscription entity is written by this command: the Connector returns Servers, the extension stores them.
A lossy import reports its lost fields; the parser never fills an unstated transport with a default.
